recommendation: Keep the commit. Future changes should only restore reference support for `:in` or `:not-in` if FHIR-I explicitly reverses the `_in` membership model.
issue_request: FHIR-36684 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5. It requested clarification of allowed search modifiers by parameter type, explicit handling for `special` search parameters, a true/false input restriction for `missing`, general modifier support rules, and correction of `combination` to `composite`.
initial_application: The main FHIR-36684 modifier clarifications are already present in `source/search.html`: the general modifier section, `special` rule, `missing` allowed-type and true/false guidance, and the modifier/type table. History shows the work spread across 2022 search-page editor commits, while the explicit FHIR-36684-tagged commit touched adjacent search/reference content rather than the core modifier matrix.
additional_context: FHIR-22690 introduced draft reference-search membership behavior for `:in`, which influenced the original FHIR-36684 table. FHIR-37846 later superseded that approach by moving membership behavior to `_in` while retaining `_list`; that issue is already represented on the combined branch by commit 410f08e1be763424d9b1528ff54d9c1c6efbf10a.
reconciliation: Changed `source/search.html` so the `not-in` summary-table type cell is `token` instead of `reference, token`. This removes a stale contradiction with the detailed `not-in` section and with the later `_in` membership mechanism.
